_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated (formative: automatically when the student clicks Generate; assessed: only via the ?teacher=1-gated action, after Final Submit). Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md §5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Accurately describes a real trend from their own data (e.g. biodiversity rose after restoring habitat or removing the invasive species; water quality or fish fell after expanding farming/fertiliser) AND gives the correct cause-and-effect mechanism behind it (fertiliser → more nutrients → algal bloom → less oxygen → fish die-off; or reduced pollution/restored habitat raised carrying capacity so populations recovered).
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine trend from the student's own recorded years, paired with an equivalent mechanism explanation; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating that 'biodiversity went up' or 'water quality dropped' with no mechanism given, or a mechanism with no trend/years referenced.

markingScheme.criterion: Recognises a DELAYED or compounding effect — that the consequence lagged the decision by one or more years, or that pressures built up over time rather than acting instantly.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct description of a lag or build-up, using their own years as evidence (e.g. 'fertiliser in Year 3 did not sink the fish population until Year 5 or 6').
markingScheme.insufficient: Describing only an immediate, same-year effect with no mention of delay or accumulation.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether the evidence supported or contradicted one of their own recorded hypotheses, gives a confidence level, and names something that would make the investigation more reliable (e.g. running it again with the opposite strategy, or repeating the same strategy to check the result holds).
markingScheme.accept: Any judgement consistent with their own data, plus any sensible reliability improvement.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating a hypothesis without judging it against the evidence, or giving a confidence level with no reliability suggestion.

markingScheme.criterion: States one specific ecological harm grounded in what the simulation showed — e.g. losing wetland area removes habitat, lowering carrying capacity/biodiversity and resilience; OR farming/housing adds nutrient runoff, lowering water quality (algae, low oxygen, fish decline), often as a delayed effect.
markingScheme.accept: Any one of: habitat/carrying-capacity loss, water-quality decline, or loss of ecosystem services (flood protection, water filtration, carbon storage, fisheries, tourism) — as long as it is linked to something the student actually saw happen in their own run.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague claim ('it will harm nature') with no specific mechanism or link to the simulation.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a SECOND, genuinely distinct ecological harm (not a restatement of the first in different words) — drawn from a different mechanism than the first point (habitat/carrying capacity, water quality, or ecosystem services).
markingScheme.accept: Any second harm from a different mechanism than the first, grounded in the simulation.
markingScheme.insufficient: A second sentence that repeats the same single idea as the first point (e.g. 'it's bad for nature' twice).

markingScheme.criterion: Suggests one sensible mitigation the town could take that trades some short-term income for long-term resilience — e.g. protect/restore part of the wetland, buffer strips or wildlife corridors, reduce fertiliser, improve wastewater treatment, limit water extraction, or phase the development.
markingScheme.accept: Any mitigation that genuinely reduces one of the harms named above while still allowing some development or income.
markingScheme.insufficient: Suggesting the town simply 'stop the project' with no partial/balanced option, or a mitigation unrelated to the harms described.

criteria.source: Auto-marked from the Knowledge Check (auto_marked_score) — the teacher does not mark this row.
= the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (trend + mechanism, delayed effect, hypothesis judgement). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No real trend identified from own data, or no mechanism given.
Identifies a real trend from own data with a plausible mechanism, but does not recognise a delayed/compounding effect, or does not compare against a recorded hypothesis.
Identifies a trend with mechanism AND recognises a delayed/compounding effect, but the hypothesis comparison, confidence level, or reliability improvement is missing or vague.

Identifies a real trend from own data with a correct cause-and-effect mechanism, recognises a delayed or compounding effect, states whether it supported/contradicted a recorded hypothesis with a confidence level, and names something that would make the investigation more reliable.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (first harm, second distinct harm, mitigation). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No credible harms given, or reasons are not based on anything observed in the simulation.
Gives one reasonable harm based on the simulation, but a second reason and/or the mitigation is missing or unconvincing.
Gives two reasonable harms based on the simulation, but the suggested mitigation is vague or does not genuinely balance benefit and protection.
Gives two reasonable harms grounded in what was actually observed in the simulation, plus one sensible mitigation that trades some short-term income for long-term resilience.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and reasoning above.

levels.descriptor: Hard to follow, or environmental-science terms are missing/incorrect.
Understandable, but with unclear phrasing or a misused term.
Clear, full sentences using correct environmental-science terminology.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (5 marks = full). Use the student's actual logged years (the action/reasoning/event/biodiversity/water/resilience columns in simulation_results.trials) to verify any trend or year the student claims to quote — do not take their prose summary on trust if it does not match their own logged data. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field, and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 13 (5 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction and one next step, all under 80 words.
